notes: Every scope carries the same four H2 headings. That is not filler: it is the structure that
defeated the scope-frequency rule (T-51, PR #127 closed unmerged). Template vocabulary
reaches every scope by construction while topical vocabulary concentrates, and a corpus
without that shape cannot measure the failure it exists to measure.
Expectations are written against this fixture and do not transfer to a real workspace.
Running the corpus elsewhere reports zero-route rate and fan-out, never recall.

Each scope owns projects/<scope>/<scope>.md, because the importer derives a document's scope from its path. Ten documents under one project would import as one scope, and the fan-out this corpus measures would have nothing to fan out across.

Each scope also carries topical H3 headings alongside the shared template. Both halves are needed: the template reproduces the vocabulary that reaches every scope, and the topical headings give the record-lexical signal something to match. A fixture with only the template measures a workspace nobody has -- record-lexical never reads body text, so all the topical content would be invisible to it and the signal would score as useless.

scopes.title: Anchor MCP
currentState: The server speaks MCP over stdio and HTTP.
decisions: The HTTP transport is the primary one; stdio is secondary.
constraints: Every tool must work on both transports.

topics.heading: Transport Parity
bullets: Both transports expose the same tool surface.

scopes.title: HTTP Transport
currentState: The HTTP transport requires a bearer token.
decisions: Rate limiting belongs in the transport, not in each tool.
constraints: Sessions expire after one hour of inactivity.

topics.heading: Bearer Token Authentication
bullets: Every request carries a bearer token.

topics.heading: Session Expiry
bullets: An idle session expires after one hour.

scopes.title: Logging
currentState: File logging is bounded by both size and retention.
decisions: Structured JSON lines, never free-form text.
constraints: No secret or credential may appear in log output.

topics.heading: Log Output Redaction
bullets: Credentials and secrets are redacted before write.

topics.heading: File Size Bounds
bullets: Rotation is driven by size and age together.

scopes.title: Claim Provenance
currentState: Every claim carries a citation to the exact source text.
decisions: A claim authored without provenance is refused.
constraints: A quote must re-resolve against the block it cites.

topics.heading: Citation Quote Resolution
bullets: A quote must re-resolve to exact offsets.

scopes.title: Retention
currentState: Telemetry is kept for ninety days and then thinned.
decisions: Retention thinning runs against telemetry, never knowledge.
constraints: Thinning must not require write access to knowledge.

topics.heading: Ninety Day Thinning
bullets: Telemetry older than ninety days is thinned.

scopes.title: Routed Retrieval
currentState: Routes are selected by path mapping, lexical match, and relation hops.
decisions: Ranking is tiered rather than weighted.
constraints: A ranker may reorder and drop, never invent.

topics.heading: Ranker Ordering
bullets: Tiers, not weights: distinct signals, then strongest.

topics.heading: Reorder And Drop, Never Invent
bullets: A ranker returns a permutation of a subset.

scopes.title: People and Teams
currentState: People and teams resolve from slack ids, emails, and display names.
decisions: A task owner is a person or a team, never a free string.
constraints: An unknown identity is an error, not an empty result.

topics.heading: Identity Resolution
bullets: Slack ids, emails and display names resolve to one person.

scopes.title: Proposed Changes
currentState: A proposal is reviewed before it is applied.
decisions: Review and apply are separate operations.
constraints: An applied proposal cannot be edited afterwards.

topics.heading: Review Before Apply
bullets: A proposal is reviewed, then applied, never both at once.

scopes.title: Telemetry
currentState: Impressions and record uses are written on every routed request.
decisions: Telemetry lives in its own schema, not in knowledge.
constraints: Telemetry writes must never fail a retrieval.

topics.heading: Separate Telemetry Schema
bullets: Retention can thin telemetry without touching knowledge.

topics.heading: Write Failure Isolation
bullets: A telemetry write must never fail a retrieval.

scopes.title: Schema Migrations
currentState: Migrations are numbered files applied in one transaction each.
constraints: A migration must be safe to apply to an existing database.

topics.heading: Forward Only Migrations
bullets: No down migrations; roll forward instead.

topics.heading: Safe On An Existing Database
bullets: Each migration must apply to a populated database.
